short: Joint normal-silent training does most of the gap closing; the viseme KL terms add 0.93 WER points with no run count reported, so the metric-learning gain is not established.
position: The paper changes training (M03): a lip-video model is trained on normal and silent recordings together, with KL terms pulling the viseme posteriors of the two modes toward each other. The verdict is standard: overt recordings already enter silent-speech training as paired-audio supervision (31 of 138 slot-filled studies), as in EMG, and the paper does not show that its loss beats those routes. Most of the reported gap closing comes from adding silent training data: the normal-to-silent WER gap falls from 10.97 to 2.70 points with cross-entropy on both modes and only to 1.77 points with the full loss. The headline gain, silent WER from 12.91% to 9.97%, is reported without a run count or spread, after a loss-weight search that does not say which split selected the weights. A later EMG study of the same idea, on a different task, reports a seed-to-seed WER standard deviation of about 1 point and used 10 seeds to show a 1.61-point gain; by that analogy the gain is not established, and run variance (M12) is not reported.
